gist: Soviet-era file cover: Фонд Дирекция имп. театров; title «Заметки дирижера на сценарий балета „Пробуждение Флоры“ (Le reveil de Flore)», франц. яз.; Начато б/д. Stamps ЦГИА ф. 497 оп. 18 ед. хр. 1191 (older number 2097? crossed out).
why: Cover only, though it names the ballet; the archivists' title calls the notes a conductor's, without naming him.

gist: Upper half of l.1, on 'Direction des Théâtres Impériaux' letterhead (eagle): French scenario headed 'Le Réveil de Flore', Scène 1 (night; Flore and her nymphs asleep, watched over by Diane; Diane disappears into the clouds) and start of Scène 2 (Entrée d'Aquilon...). The scenario is in a faint, fluent hand. In the left margin a second, darker hand has bracketed passages and written musical labels: 'Nocturne' (Scène 1), 'musique de scène' (Scène 2), and a word that may be 'Sostenuto?'. No signature on the page. The darker hand assigning numbers and tempi to scenario passages fits a composer's or conductor's working plan, which is consistent with Дриго (who composed the 1894 ballet). But nothing on the page names him, and his hand was not compared.
why: Working document for the 1894 ballet Пробуждение Флоры: a scenario with a musical plan written in the margins.

gist: Lower half of l.1; overlaps p.2 from 'Diane disparaît dans les nuages' / Scène 2. Rest of Scène 2: Aquilon's entry, Flore's nymphs, Aurore(?) to come and wake Flore. Margin, dark hand: 'musique de scène', a word possibly 'Sostenuto?', then 'Scherzo' bracketing the later part of Scène 2. No signature.
why: The marginal musical plan for Пробуждение Флоры continues (Scherzo).

gist: Verso of l.1 (the letterhead eagle shows through, mirrored, top left). Scène 3: Aurore appears, consoles Flore, Apollon is announced (corrections in the text). Scène 4: the god of day (Apollon) restores life with his rays and kisses Flore; Zéphyre(?). Margin, dark hand: 'mus. scène I?', then 'Adagio?' struck through and replaced by 'Valse lente'; 'Scène' struck through, then 'musique de Scène'; a monogram-like scribble. No signature.
why: Numbers assigned for the 1894 ballet (Valse lente replacing an Adagio). Shows the music being planned against the scenario.

gist: Lower view of the same verso; overlaps p.4 from Scène 4. Text continues: Cupidon and the Amours(?) play with Flore's nymphs; Zéphyre. Margin, dark hand: 'musique de Scène', the scribble, then a bracketed group 'Pizzicato', 'gavotte', 'pas d'action' (struck through), 'adage', 'Variations', 'coda valse': in effect a grand pas structure. No signature.
why: Most detailed musical layout in the file: pizzicato, gavotte, adage, variations, coda valse for Пробуждение Флоры.

gist: L.2 (the numeral '2' is written over struck-out words, top right). Scène 5: Mercure(?), messenger of the gods, brings Jupiter's order to Flore and Zéphyre(?) and offers the cup of youth / eternal life; Hébé(?) brings the divine beverage. Scène 6: Cortège de Bacchus, Sylvains, satyres; Grande bacchanale (insertion about bacchantes / Bacchus and Ariane). Scène 7: Apothéose: gloire des dieux. Margin, dark hand: 'musique de Scène' (written vertically); 'marche' struck through and replaced by 'bacchanale'; 'adage'; 'galop furioso?'; 'Largo'. No signature.
why: Final scenes and the apotheosis with their musical plan (bacchanale, galop, Largo) for Пробуждение Флоры.

gist: Lower view of l.2; duplicates p.6 from the middle of Scène 5 through Scène 7 'Apothéose'. The rest of the leaf is blank. Same marginal annotations: bacchanale (replacing marche), adage, galop, Largo. No signature anywhere in the file; the end of the text is unsigned.
why: Duplicate view of p.6. It confirms the document ends at the Apothéose with no signature.
